name: Genoise
origin: Named for Genoa, Italy, but codified as a whipped whole-egg sponge in French patisserie training since the 19th century; the base of countless French layered cakes (fraisier, opera, Black Forest gateau).

ingredients.note: melted butter folded in last, off the whipped-egg foam's heat, per the classic genoise method

process.name: whip eggs and sugar
process.description: whip whole eggs with sugar over a bain-marie to about 40 C, then off the heat to full ribbon-stage volume

process.name: fold in flour
process.description: sift and fold flour into the whipped egg foam in stages, minimising deflation of the incorporated air

process.name: fold in butter
process.description: fold in cooled melted butter last, a small volume against a large foam

process.name: bake
process.description: bake in a buttered and floured round pan

notes: Flour:sugar:egg:butter close to 100:100:166:20 is the classic genoise proportion set out in Wayne Gisslen, Professional Baking, ch. 'Cakes and Icings' (sponge/foam method): egg mass roughly 1.5-1.7x flour mass, with only a light butter enrichment folded in at the end, distinguishing it from a butter (creaming-method) cake. No chemical leavening: the whipped-egg foam is the only aeration mechanism, matching real practice.
